title: Tripod — Podcast Player
summary: Tripod is a brand new podcast app designed to make it easy to stay up to date with your favourite shows. It’s built around an inbox for new episodes and queues for what you’re listening to. Audio & Playback Tripod has integrated EQ settings, can trim silence, and balance audio levels across episodes, for the smoothest listening experience. You can skip chapters or use the transcript to jump to a specific line. It also has an innovative playback scrubber that snaps to the starts of chapters, glides over skipped chapters, and uses haptic feedback for extra precision. Inbox The inbox is where new episodes arrive and you can decide whether to keep or ignore episodes. For the shows where you listen to every episode, you can send them straight to the queue. Queues Instead of playlists you have to manually manage, Tripod has automatic queues. There’s a main queue, favourites, shorts, in-progress, and each genre gets its own queue. There’s also a special queue called Someday, which lets you keep episodes that you know you want to listen to, but you don’t need to be reminded of every time you open the app. It’s ideal for podcasts discussing books or movies that you haven’t seen yet. Innovative Controls Building on decade of experience with Obscura, my award-winning camera app, Tripod uses haptics and gestures to create delightful interactions throughout the app. Intelligence On supported devices, Tripod will use Apple Intelligence to transcribe episodes, generate chapters, and determine hosts and guests for the shows you listen to, and even recommended other shows that they’ve guested on. Appearance Every view and control in Tripod is designed to adapt its appearance to what you’re listening to, making the app feel personal and vibrant. You can also choose a tint color or make the whole app monochrome if you prefer. There’s also a few app icon choices to best fit your Home Screen. Apple Watch Tripod has an Apple Watch companion app that lets you control what you listen to, skip chapters and change audio settings. Handy, or should I say… wristy? CarPlay Tripod also has a CarPlay app so you can drive safe while listening to what moves you. Well the car moves you. But art can also move you. Are podcasts not art? Who is to say. Shortcuts & Intents For the automation sickos, Tripod has actions for controlling playback and audio settings, getting and editing the contents of your queues and inbox, and more. Widgets Yeah. It’s got widgets too. Yeah, for your Home Screen! Spotlight Integration Quickly find your shows from anywhere on your device. Sleep Timers Time based or end of chapter or end of episode. And so much more. ———— Privacy Policy: http://benricemccarthy.com/tripod/privacy Terms of use: http://benricemccarthy.com/tripod/terms

title: Mushroom FM
summary: Mushroom FM, the Home of the Fun Guys, brings you four decades of magic Mushroom memories: music from the 50s to the 80s, presented live by a friendly team from New Zealand, Australia, Britain, South Africa, Canada and the US. Commercial-free, apart from the occasional old advert played for nostalgia. Built for VoiceOver from the start. Many of our presenters and listeners are blind or partially sighted, so every screen is designed to be quick and easy with VoiceOver, as well as for sighted listeners. LISTEN LIVE - Mushroom FM at the press of a button, with the show, the presenter and the song playing now. - Pause live radio and carry on where you left off, or go back to the start of the show. - Keeps playing with your iPhone locked, with controls on the Lock Screen and your headphones. - A sleep timer, including "end of this show". MUSHROOM ESCAPE Our old-time radio channel: drama, comedy, mystery and science fiction from the golden age of radio, from America, the BBC and beyond, scheduled by hand so your favourite series is on at the same time every week. SCHEDULE AND REMINDERS See the week's shows on both channels, and get a reminder before the shows you don't want to miss. LISTEN AGAIN Missed a show? Play recent shows again. TALK TO THE PRESENTERS Send a written or recorded message to the presenter on air, or to any of the Fun Guys. If you're on Mastodon, toot the presenter and follow what the Mushroom Crowd is saying, right in the app. AND MORE - Siri: "Play Mushroom FM" and "Play Mushroom FM Escape". - A Home Screen widget. - An Apple Watch app that plays the live stream. Mushroom FM is a licensed internet radio station.

title: Bambu Handy
summary: Remotely control your Bambu Lab 3D printers, explore MakerWorld’s vast library of free models, and print your favorite designs with one tap！ Remote Printer Control - Remotely operate the machine to start and stop printing whenever needed - Get real-time printing status and resolve errors promptly - Access to learning resources and step-by-step instructions to fix printing problems - High-resolution live view of the printing process - Automatic records of the printing process to help diagnose printing failures - Automatic timelapse video of the printing process to share with others 3D Model Discovery with MakerWorld - Explore countless creative models and enjoy high-quality printing for free - Find trendy works and customize your unique models with MakerLab - Like, collect, and print in one tap to bring your ideas to life - Interact with makers and redeem credits for Bambu products Bambu Handy is a free 3D printing platform. We are open to any feedback and suggestions. Whether you are an expert, hobbyist or newcomer, we would like to grow together with you. Contact: https://support.bambulab.com/en

title: Word Burner: Daily Chain
summary: A daily word chain against the clock. Every word starts on the last letter of the one before, and every letter you start a word with burns. Land on a burnt letter and the fire goes out. Everyone gets the same puzzle each day, and you get one scored run. Two minutes. How far can you chain? A NEW TWIST EVERY DAY The week gets harder from Monday to Sunday: • Monday, Classic: the plain rules • Tuesday, Hot letter: one letter is on fire, and words with it score triple • Wednesday, Long burn: words of seven or more letters score double • Thursday, Slow burn: start with one minute, and every word adds five seconds • Friday, Ashes: three letters start already burned • Saturday, Bonfire: every word needs five letters or more • Sunday, Inferno: Ashes and Bonfire together FEATURES • A fresh puzzle every day, the same for every player in the world • A bonus letter that comes back to life once you've played 40 letters • Daily and weekly Game Center leaderboards: today's best run, and your week added up from Monday to Sunday. Rank against everyone, or just your friends • Every twist explained in How to play, so you know what Sunday's Inferno has in store • Share your result as a card that shows your score and the shape of your round, never your words, so nobody gets spoiled • Streaks that grow every day you play • Satisfying burn effects and sound, made for quick sessions • No ads, no accounts, no tracking. Your progress stays on your phone WORD BURNER PRO One purchase, no subscription: practice any twist as often as you like, replay every past daily, and see your full stats. The daily, the leaderboards, your streak and sharing are always free, and Pro never changes the scored daily.

title: Tact: Find It by Touch
summary: A haptic game you play by touch, without looking at the screen. The screen is black glass. Feel for the one place that is different, and break it. Tap anywhere with one to five fingers, the way you'd play a piano. Each tap answers with a small tick under your fingertip. Somewhere, one place feels different: a little longer, a double tap, or a little harder. When you find it, keep tapping it. A crack runs across the glass, and it breaks, with a deep haptic, a short high glass sound and a soft light. Play it absent-mindedly, with the TV on. Each pane you break still feels like a small win. While you play, no score appears on screen. Numbers show only when you pause, when a Time Attack run ends, or when a pane breaks in a Duel. FOUR WAYS TO PLAY • Calm: No time limit, no score. Find the one place that feels different, and keep breaking the glass • Standard: Each pane you break makes the difference a little subtler (12 levels). If you can't find it, it becomes clearer again. Pause to see your current level and your best • Time Attack: How many panes can you break while the line goes once around the screen in 60 seconds? Cues at the start, every 15 seconds and in the last 3 seconds. Your best is kept • Duel: Two players, one iPhone laid between you, face to face. Each of you has a place of your own that feels different (longer or double tap). Whoever's place breaks first scores, even if the other player broke it. First to 1, 3, 5 or 7 RECORDS • Your best level in Standard and your best count in Time Attack • Records made with Stronger Difference or Sound Hints on are kept apart as assisted records MAKE IT YOURS • Haptic Strength: Gentle, Standard or Strong • Sound volume, and Tap Sound • Touch Trace, and Completion Light (Off, Soft or Bright) • Taps to Break: 5, 7, 10 or 12 (10 to start) • Settings are under the faint gear that appears at the top right when you pause. While playing, hold two fingers for two seconds, then lift them GETTING STARTED • On first launch, a short tutorial of about 30 seconds, on a bigger 2×3 grid • Watch it again any time with Replay Tutorial in Settings FOR EVERYONE • Playable with VoiceOver. The play area takes your taps directly, and the tutorial text, the time left and results in Time Attack, level changes, and points and wins in a Duel are read aloud • Stronger Difference makes the difference clearer and uses only the two clearest kinds • With Sound Hints on, the place that feels different also sounds a little different • Reduce Animation makes broken pieces fade where they are instead of falling. Reduce Motion in iOS Settings is respected too • The whole screen never flashes bright white SOUND • Sounds play along with your music or TV. They don't stop other audio • No sound in Silent Mode. You can play without sound MADE FOR IPHONE HAPTICS • Tact is played by feel, so it is best on iPhone • On devices without haptics, such as iPad, you find the different place by sound (turn the sound on, and turn Silent Mode off) YOURS, ON YOUR IPHONE • No account, and no network connection • Settings and records stay on this iPhone • No ads, no in-app purchases, no tracking Requires an iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Available in English, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Korean, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese (Brazil).

title: Game World: Accessible Games
summary: Play Dominoes, Ludo, word games and more with friends. Blind, low-vision and sighted players can play together with VoiceOver support. Join friends in Dominoes and Ludo, challenge computer opponents, or enjoy a game on your own. Explore 10 games: • Dominoes — Challenge friends or computer opponents, or sharpen your skills in practice mode. • Ludo — Race your pawns home in this classic board game with other players or computer opponents. • Blackjack — Take on the dealer in the classic game of 21. • Video Poker — Play five-card draw, choose which cards to hold, and chase a Royal Flush. • Word Builder — Discover hidden words in a wheel of letters. • Hangman — Solve word puzzles one guess at a time. • Trivia Trail — Test your knowledge with timed or untimed play. • Simon — Remember and repeat increasingly challenging sequences. • Battle Cats — Find hidden words in letter grids and explore themed puzzles at your own pace. • Craps — Learn with guided solo practice and spoken roll results. Designed for accessible play: • VoiceOver navigation and spoken gameplay feedback. • Themes and sound settings to personalize your game room. • Multiplayer, computer opponents, and solo experiences across the game collection. • In-game chat to stay connected while you play. From AppA11y, the team behind Dice World and Card World. Download Game World and find your next favorite game. Gold Membership is an auto-renewable subscription. title: Boat Hunter
summary: Year 2077. The Atlantic Ocean no longer separates continents. It watches them. For decades, the world learned to smile while sharpening its teeth. Europe and Asia forged an alliance. The American bloc answered with steel, satellites, and fortified trade routes. No one declared open war. No one had to. Peace remained in the speeches, on the screens, and in the treaties. But on the high seas, the truth took another form. The cargo ships never stopped sailing. Food, fuel, minerals, data, weapons—everything kept crossing the ocean under legal flags and flawless orders. Only one thing changed. There are no captains anymore. Now the ships think. Every convoy, every armed destroyer, every autonomous freighter, and every ocean hunter is commanded by artificial intelligences trained to calculate, anticipate, and survive. War no longer needs hatred. It only needs algorithms better than the enemy’s. And you are the finest algorithm ever deployed. You are the most advanced naval combat unit ever built: the fastest hull, the sharpest sensors, the deadliest tactical architecture. You do not sleep. You do not hesitate. You do not forget. Where others detect noise, you see patterns. Where others see waves, you read intentions. Where others react, you have already decided. Your mission is simple to state and nearly impossible to execute: protect your routes, intercept threats, dominate the Atlantic. But the ocean does not forgive mistakes. In its waters travel allies, enemies, and machines that have not yet decided what they will become when the final order arrives. Every radar echo may be a freighter. Every silence may be an ambush. Every encounter may be the beginning of a war the world still insists on denying. There are no heroes here. No parades. No witnesses. Only steel, fog, encrypted signals, and decisions made at the speed of death. On this sea, peace is a display. War is what you are. Welcome to the Atlantic. Enter combat! ---------- Boat Hunter is an accessible naval action and strategy game set in the North Atlantic. You control an autonomous warship on a patrol of consecutive missions, where every decision can put the next operation at risk. MASTER THE OCEAN • Navigate the tactical map, set your heading, and interpret contacts, signals, and radio messages. • Identify allies and enemies: armed ships, merchant vessels, submarines, oil platforms, and floating bases. • Fight at close range with your autocannon and torpedoes. • Repair damage, deploy smoke screens, and decide when to disengage. EVERY MISSION DEMANDS A STRATEGY Reach coordinates, clear hostile sectors, intercept convoys, sink merchant tonnage, defend positions, rescue allies, resupply, and destroy floating targets. Sea conditions, time limits, and enemy behavior will force you to adapt your plans. UPGRADE YOUR SHIP Earn money and score points by completing objectives and sinking enemies. Between missions, upgrade your hull, engine, weapons, damage control, smoke screen, and gunner systems. Higher-quality enemies are more dangerous, but grant greater rewards. Keep your remaining money to begin your next game with an advantage. LEARN AT YOUR OWN PACE A three-mission tutorial teaches you to navigate, aim, and survive. Read the manual and listen to every signal in the sound guide before entering combat. Play visually or through sound and VoiceOver. Choose from three difficulty levels: Deckhand, Captain, and Admiral. Complete as many missions as possible, keep your ship operational, and beat your best score. ---------- This app supports VoiceOver, Zoom, and other iOS accessibility features. If you encounter an accessibility problem, please contact us so we can fix it. Accessibility should be the foundation of a project, not a patch applied to the product.

title: Atomicom
summary: Space is young, dark and scattered. Atoms drift alone, touching nothing, and in all that emptiness not one thing has ever been built. No water. No stone. No star with a planet worth the name. That is what you are here to change. Atomicom is a puzzle game about binding matter together. Atoms come to you one at a time. Place them on the board, let their loose electrons find a partner, and when every electron in a connected group has one, the molecule is finished: it holds, it leaves the board, and the universe keeps a piece of itself that did not exist a moment ago. HOW IT PLAYS • An atom arrives in the glass cylinder below the board. Take it and drop it on any free square. • Atoms bond with the neighbours above, below, left and right of them. Never diagonally. • A green atom has one electron to give, yellow has two, orange three, red four. Blue atoms give nothing at all: they only take up room you were going to need. • Satisfy every electron in a connected group and the molecule forms and goes. • Run out of squares, or let the cylinder overflow, and the mission ends there. 300 MISSIONS The board starts wide and gets smaller: twelve squares across, then ten, then eight, then a six by six where there is nowhere left to be careless. Every mission asks more than the one before it — more molecules, more obstacles in the way, heavier atoms that need more neighbours before they are satisfied — and every time the board shrinks you begin again at something gentle and climb back up. MADE TO BE PLAYED BY EVERYONE Atomicom is made by Tyflos Accessible Software. Accessibility here is not a switch in the settings, it is how the game is built. • Fully playable with VoiceOver, from the first tap to the last molecule. Nothing has to be seen. • Every square tells you its coordinate, what is on it and how many electrons are still free: "A2, red, 3 free bonds". • The sound tells you where. An atom bonding on the left is heard on the left, and the top of the board sounds higher than the bottom, so the board has a shape you can hear. • Everything that happens without you touching it is spoken: an atom arriving, a molecule finished, a move the rules will not allow and why not. • Vibration answers every move, soft for an atom placed and hard for a molecule completed. • Drag if you like, or tap the atom and then the square. Both always work. • Dynamic Type throughout, and Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency are obeyed. • Choose your own background, square borders and cylinder colour, and the game tells you when a colour you picked is too faint to make out. ALSO • Play in seventeen languages. • Made for iPhone and iPad. • Your game saves itself: leave in the middle of a mission and pick it up later. • A table of your best games, kept on your device. FREE, AND WHAT COSTS MONEY • The first ten missions are free, with advertising. • "All levels" is a one-off purchase that opens the three hundred. The advertising stays. • "No ads" is a second one-off purchase that removes the banner. It needs "All levels" first. The universe is not going to assemble itself. Start with two atoms.

title: Top Tech Tidbits
summary: Top Tech Tidbits is a free weekly newsletter on access technology for people who are blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled. Founded in 2004 and read by over 48,000 people each week, it gathers human-curated news, tips and how-tos every Thursday morning. The app opens the newest issue the moment you open it, and keeps recent issues, and every older issue you open, on your iPhone and iPad, so you can read with no connection. MADE FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION READERS FIRST • Built for VoiceOver and braille: every section and tidbit is a heading, every control is named, and Apple's accessibility audit checks every main screen in every version. • Larger Text up to the largest sizes, Light and Dark, Bold Text, the Atkinson Hyperlegible font, high-contrast colors and wider line spacing. • Listen: your iPhone reads the issue aloud in the voice and speed you choose, keeps reading when the screen locks, skips a whole section at a time, and stops on a sleep timer. Listen to all your saved tidbits in a row. • "Hey Siri, read me the latest Top Tech Tidbits" and "Hey Siri, search Top Tech Tidbits". • Keyboard commands for a keyboard connected to your iPhone or iPad. EVERY ISSUE SINCE 2008 • Past Issues lists this year's issues, then every earlier year back to 2008. • Search every issue from 2008 to today, tidbit by tidbit, even with no connection, and find tidbits from the iPhone's own search. • Topic Alerts: follow words or names, such as JAWS or braille, and get an alert when a new issue mentions them. Your iPhone looks through the issue itself, so your topics never reach us; only your own Apple devices and your iCloud account have them. • Events lists the upcoming events from the issues, soonest first; add any of them to your calendar in two taps. • A link to an issue, in an email or a message, opens right in the app at the tidbit it points to. • Stories open in Reader View: just their words, without the website's menus and ads. • Translate an issue into another language with Apple's own translation, on your device (iOS 18 or later). KEEP, NOTE AND SHARE • Save tidbits for later, add your own notes, and highlight passages; VoiceOver and braille say where each highlight starts and ends. All of it follows you to your other Apple devices through your iCloud account, with your settings and the place you left each issue. • Share any tidbit with a link that opens the issue right at it, or share a whole issue as a link, a text file or an EPUB book for the Books app or a braille notetaker. • Send Top Tech Tidbits a story from any app's Share button. ALWAYS THE NEWEST • An optional notification each Thursday, normally at 6:00 AM Eastern, with a Listen button; the issue is already downloaded, ready to read. A 1 on the app's icon means a new issue you have not opened yet. • Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, a Control Center button that starts Listen (iOS 18 or later), and shortcuts on the app's icon. • On iPad, the issue's sections or your saved tidbits sit beside the issue. PRIVACY No account, no advertising added by the app, and no tracking. To learn what readers find most useful the app keeps anonymous counts of which issues and tidbits are opened; you can turn them off in Settings. Details: https://toptechtidbits.com/app-privacy/ Questions and ideas: publisher@toptechtidbits.com

title: I Have a Garden
summary: One zucchini plant. 48 real days. Here the game's time is your time. You water it tonight and by tomorrow the soil will be a little drier. It gets light and dark at the same time as it does outside your window. The stems, the leaves and the flowers are drawn by an algorithm that imitates how a plant really grows. No two games give you the same shape, or the same harvest. Once you have the zucchini figured out, try the tomato plant: twice the days, up to twenty tomatoes, suckers to prune and a plant that climbs tied to its stake. It brings its own seeds, its own chimera tomato and new achievements. And for a third challenge, the pepper plant: 72 days, and snails that climb the stem to eat its leaves and peppers, which you pick off with your gloves. Each pepper turns from green to yellow to red, and you have to pick it at the right moment. It brings its own chimera pepper, its own seeds and new achievements. You unlock it with a single purchase, which also removes the ads. All three plants grow at the same time, each in its own plot. WHAT YOU'LL DO You check on it, water or feed it if it's time, look for pests and pull the odd weed. For as long as you feel like. HOW THE CYCLE GOES You start by preparing the soil and burying the seed. Until flowering you have to look after it as well as you can, because that stretch decides how many flowers open. When they do, the bees arrive to pollinate them, and if you've kept it up, every one sets fruit. The last stretch takes the most attention: each zucchini has its right moment, and picking it early or leaving it too long costs you points. IMPROVE YOUR PLANT When the cycle ends, you can take the seeds out of the Prime and Overripe zucchini you harvested. There are four qualities: Wild, Adapted, Selected and Heirloom. The better the seed, the more main branches the stem puts out. That raises your chances of getting a chimera zucchini, the hardest thing in the game to pull off. ACHIEVEMENTS There are twenty-seven achievements to earn along the way, gardener's ranks among them: when you gather the harvest you get a score and the rank you earned with the plant. WHAT IT DOESN'T DO No account, no email. No lives, no paying your way forward: the only purchase is the pepper plant, and it's optional. No leaderboard, nobody to beat. And it doesn't message you for the sake of it: a notification arrives when the plant actually needs something, at most one a day, not every evening at seven. It's free and kept going by advertising. If you'd rather support it another way, the pepper purchase removes the ads for good. ALSO You can put a widget on your home screen with the water and feed gauges, without opening the game. A notebook inside that explains every mechanic with real numbers, if you want to know why. A daily graph of water, feed and pests since the day you planted the seed. And a few more surprises. Thank you for playing.
